description: How people use the app: screens, taps, paths, features, funnels and return rates. Anonymous (random install_id only). Needs app build 25+.

panels.title: Top screens
panels.description: Bad: a screen you expect to be popular with few views is hard to reach, or a surprising one dominates; review navigation.

panels.title: Top taps
panels.description: Bad: key actions with few taps are not discoverable; move or relabel them. Only registry taps are counted.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (target) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="tap"} | json target="props.target" [$__range])))

panels.title: Feature usage
panels.description: Bad: a feature nobody uses may be hidden or broken; check its entry point and error rate.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (feature) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="feature_used"} | json feature="props.feature" [$__range])))

panels.title: Screen views over time (top 8)
panels.description: Bad: a screen whose views collapse after a release became unreachable; check navigation and unexpected redirects.

panels.title: Paths between screens (Loki; see the note)
How paths are computed
panels.description: Bad: not a metric; LogQL cannot join consecutive events, so there is no screen->screen Sankey. Use the panels below as approximations and see OPERATIONS.md.

options.content:
**Paths: honest limits.** LogQL cannot join one event to the next, so true screen -> screen counts need an external job.

- *Entry screens*: first `screen_view` of a session (t < 3 s) - where people land.
- *Session path explorer*: paste one `session_id` into the variable above to read that session's screens in order.
- *Unexpected redirects*: exact from -> to pairs (they are explicit events).
- *Screens per session*: depth of use, bucketed.

panels.title: Entry screens (first screen of a session)
panels.description: Bad: if a deep screen is the main entry, deep links or the home tab are not doing their job; review the first-run path.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (screen) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="screen_view"} | json screen="screen", t="t" | t < 3000 [$__range])))

panels.title: Unexpected redirects: from -> to
panels.description: Bad: any row is a user bounced to the wrong place (e.g. Services -> onboarding); fix the guard named by the reason.

targets.expr: sum by (from, to, reason) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="nav_unexpected_redirect"} | json from="props.from", to="props.to", reason="props.reason" [$__range]))

panels.title: Session path explorer (screens in order)
panels.description: Bad: a path that bounces back and forth or stops at an error is the pattern to fix; paste a session_id above (empty shows recent sessions).

targets.expr: {job="pawpi-client", event="screen_view"} | json session_id="session_id", screen="screen" | session_id=~"${session}.*" | line_format "{{.session_id}} {{.screen}}"

panels.description: Bad: a step far below the one before it is where people give up (activation steps count once per install); open that screen/flow and fix the friction.

panels.description: Bad: a low % means most people stop between those two steps (above 100% = the step repeats per user); fix the screen between them first.

panels.title: D1 return
panels.description: Bad: below 20% means few of yesterday's users come back today; improve reminders and first-run value. Needs 2 days of Loki retention.

targets.expr: 100 * count(sum by (install_id) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="session_start"} | json install_id="install_id" [1d])) and sum by (install_id) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="session_start"} | json install_id="install_id" [1d] offset 1d))) / count(sum by (install_id) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="session_start"} | json install_id="install_id" [1d] offset 1d)))

panels.description: Bad: low means few people active 7 day(s) ago are active now; improve habit loops (reminders, digest). Needs 8+ days of Loki retention, so free-tier Loki cannot show it.

panels.description: Bad: a shrinking number means fewer people use the app; distinct anonymous installs, capped near 500 by Loki series limits.

panels.description: Bad: one platform collapsing means a platform-specific break; check that platform's latest build.

panels.title: How D1/D7/D30 are computed
panels.description: Bad: not a metric; return rate is only as good as Loki retention, so a blank D7/D30 usually means retention, not zero return.

options.content:
**Return rate = share of installs active N days ago that are active again today.**

LogQL: `count(A and A offset Nd) / count(A offset Nd)` where `A = sum by (install_id) (count_over_time({job="pawpi-client", event="session_start"} | json install_id="install_id" [1d]))`.

Limits: it is rolling-activity retention, not a first-seen install cohort (LogQL cannot find an install's first event). It needs Loki to hold N+1 days of logs (Grafana Cloud free keeps about 14 days: D1 and D7 work, **D30 needs longer retention**). Loki caps a query at ~500 series by default, so above ~500 active installs per day use shorter ranges or move the calculation to a recording rule.
